text: Shawnee Slopes is a residential neighbourhood located in the southwest quadrant of Calgary, Alberta, Canada, bordered to the south by James McKevitt Road, to the east by Macleod Trail, to the north by Fish Creek Provincial Park, and to the west by Evergreen Street SW. The neighbourhood is named after the Shawnee native people and is represented in the Calgary City Council by Ward 13 councillors. At its center lies the Shawnee Slopes Golf Course, which served as a primary amenity for residents and the public. On 13 June 2011, it was announced that the golf course would permanently close to the public on 2 October 2011. In February 2013, the city council approved the redevelopment of the golf course lands to construct 1,400 new homes. Shawnee Slopes is closely linked to the northern section of the adjacent Evergreen community, sharing the same community association, while the remainder of Evergreen operates independently. According to the City of Calgary's 2012 municipal census, Shawnee Slopes had a population of 1,565 living in 866 dwellings, representing a 2.4% increase from its 2011 population of 1,529. With a land area of 1.2 km² (0.46 sq mi), the population density was 1,300/km² (3,380/sq mi) in 2012. In 2005, residents had a median household income of $106,379, with 3.4% living in low-income households; in 2006, 26.9% of residents were immigrants. Additionally, 12.9% of the buildings were condominiums or apartments, and 1.6% of the housing was used for renting.
